answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before trading, recorded in a shared atlas of deposits. If a grading jury catches an identity submitting fake work, its stake is slashed and redistributed to honest participants. An attacker wanting a thousand fake accounts must therefore fund a thousand stakes, turning a cheap lagoon of throwaway identities into a costly venture. Honest agents recover their deposit in full, so the scheme is an oasis of safety for legitimate newcomers: fraud becomes expensive while good behavior stays nearly free.
